- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 2–3% below peak or adjust downward by 2–5% in next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; apply downward correction proportional to sentiment drop (e.g., 0.5x sentiment drop = 0.5x price correction).
- Model underperforms in early horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply smoothing or lagged sentiment-weighted average for first 3–5 periods.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted median or trimmed mean to reduce noise.
- If true outcome deviates >5% from forecast in first 3 days, assume model is misaligned with sentiment trend; re-calibrate forecast using sentiment history as anchor.
